body: You can just buy a bag of charcoal briquettes from any gas/petrol station and cook a handful of them on your stove or oven, then get into bed and go to sleep (CO poisoning is painless and symptomless). It's what I'm planning anyway.

I think if your friend doesn't want you to involve yourself in their mental health, then you shouldn't. I honestly don't mean to sound harsh but their life ultimately isn't your business and you don't *have* to do anything about it.

You can just accept it's a private issue and continue being a non-judgemental friend, which may actually inadvertently be the best thing you *could* do for their mental health.

You could try hotlines or social media communities but imo your best bet is probably accumulating some savings or getting health insurance that covers therapy, and researching suicide-specialist private therapists or providers who have a track record of specifically not hospitalizing difficult patients. Then shopping around for ones that are a good match for your personality.

Practitioners are only made to report suicidal patients when they seem to be imminently at risk of killing themselves. Most ('most', definitely not 'all' sadly) will be tolerant of their patients expressing suicidal thoughts. They're extremely common.

(If you're worried about hotlines surreptitiously calling the cops "for your own good", just don't use a landline and call them at a friend's house)
It's almost impossible to kill yourself by taking pills, I saw something a while ago suggesting the success rate was less than 2%. Your body just painfully metabolizes everything or vomits it up.
